passage:
A small shop sold soap, shampoo, rice, and beans without disposable packaging. Customers brought their own bottles and containers.
At first, shopping there took longer. Customers had to weigh containers and write labels. But many liked reducing waste.
The owner said the shop was not for everyone, but it showed another way to buy daily goods.
A student compared prices and found some items cheaper, others more expensive. Her report explained both benefits and limits.
The refill shop was not a perfect solution. It was a practical experiment.
Changing habits requires systems that make better choices possible, not just good intentions.
